components.description: Published posts, paged, read in the background and streamed in: one category, one tag, the words a reader searched for, one language or the whole archive. As a grid of cards, or as a compact list for a sidebar.

helpers.name: trimmed
helpers.code:
# A VALUE THAT IS NOT TEXT IS NO TEXT. `search` and `tag` come off the query string, where
# `?q[a]=b` is a map and `?tag[]=x` a list: either is nothing asked, as the search box reads a
# `q` that is not a string.

  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  scalar when is_atom(scalar) or is_number(scalar) -> to_string(scalar)
  _map_or_list -> ""

helpers.name: slug_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

helpers.name: missing!
helpers.code:
# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

helpers.name: narrow
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

query = narrow_language(query, asked.language)

query =
  case asked.featured_only do
    true -> Ash.Query.filter(query, featured == true)
    false -> query
  end

# THE ROW THE HEADING NAMES IS THE ROW THE LIST IS OF. A slug is unique per SITE and not per
# language, so `filter_row/1` resolves it in the page's language — and narrowed by the slug alone
# this listed the Persian posts filed under an English category beneath the page's fallback
# heading, having just decided that category does not exist in Persian. Empty and `all` narrow
# nothing, the same two answers `only_language/2` gives.
query =
  case {asked.collection, asked.language} do
    {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
      query

    {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
      Ash.Query.filter(
        query,
        exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active and language == ^code)
      )

    {wanted, _every_language} ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active))
  end

query =
  case {asked.tag, asked.language} do
    {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
      query

    {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted and language == ^code))

    {wanted, _every_language} ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted))
  end

# THE WORDS A READER TYPED, matched in the title and in the summary, whatever their case — what the
# search box on the blog's home asks for.
query =
  case asked.search do
    "" ->
      query

    term ->
      found = Ash.CiString.new(term)
      Ash.Query.filter(query, contains(title, ^found) or contains(excerpt, ^found))
  end

query =
  case asked.exclude_featured do
    0 -> query
    count -> Ash.Query.filter(query, not (id in ^featured_ids(asked, count, source)))
  end

case asked.exclude_slug do
  "" -> query
  wanted -> Ash.Query.filter(query, slug != ^wanted)
end

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A ROW NAMED BY SLUG IS NARROWED BY THE PAGE'S LANGUAGE, NOT BY THE EDITION RULE. A slug names
# one category or one tag per site whatever language it is written in, so the master-editions
# default `narrow_language/2` applies to a listing would be meaningless here — while no narrowing
# at all headed /fa/blog/category/<english slug> with the English category's name, over the nothing
# that category holds in Persian.
require Ash.Query

case trimmed(wanted) do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: filter_row
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

# THE ROW THE LIST IS OF, when a category or a tag narrows it: the heading's words, and for a tag
# the words of the chip that says so. A tag's row is read for the chip even when the page gives the
# list a heading of its own.
row =
  cond do
    asked.collection != "" and asked.show_filter_title ->
      {:collection,
       shared_row(source, "blog:category", asked) ||
         MishkaBlog.Collection
         |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
         |> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^asked.collection)
         |> only_language(asked.language)
         |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :description])
         |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
         |> first_row()}

    asked.tag != "" and (asked.show_filter_title or asked.tagged_text != "") ->
      {:tag,
       shared_row(source, "blog:tag", asked) ||
         MishkaBlog.Tag
         |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
         |> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^asked.tag)
         |> only_language(asked.language)
         |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :description])
         |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
         |> first_row()}

    true ->
      {nil, nil}
  end

# TITLED, when the list is headed with the row's own name: a category's always, a tag's unless the
# page gave a heading for tags of its own, which is what the design's chip under it is for.
case row do
  {_kind, nil} ->
    nil

  {kind, found} ->
    %{
      kind: kind,
      name: found.name,
      description: found.description,
      titled: asked.show_filter_title and (kind == :collection or asked.tag_heading == "")
    }
end

helpers.name: shared_row
helpers.code:
# THE CATEGORY OR THE TAG THE PAGE IS OF, as the page read it once for its head and its blocks, when
# it handed it down for this reader and it is the one this list is narrowed by; `nil` where it is
# not, and the row is read here. A category or a tag the reader may not open is no row either way.
slug =
  case kind do
    "blog:category" -> asked.collection
    "blog:tag" -> asked.tag
  end

case shared(source, {:record, kind, slug, asked.language}) do
  {:ok, %{} = row} -> row
  _not_shared -> nil
end

helpers.name: posts_page
helpers.code:
# HOW MANY POSTS THE LIST PAGES THROUGH is the page's own count where the page read it once for its
# search box too (`shared_total/2`), and only the page of posts is read; else Ash counts them beside
# the page.
#
# THE PAGE OF POSTS ITSELF is the page's own where the page read exactly this one, as cards, for this
# reader (`shared_page/4`): on the front page it read them with the strip's, so what their cards
# are drawn from was loaded once for both.
total = shared_total(asked, source)

case {shared_page(asked, page, per_page, source), total} do
  {{:ok, rows}, {:ok, counted}} -> {:ok, %{rows: rows, total: counted}}
  _read_here -> read_page(asked, page, per_page, source, total)
end

helpers.name: read_page
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

# WHAT A CARD IS DRAWN FROM comes with the post: the name of the first category it is filed under,
# in the statement that reads the posts, and the people who wrote it, each read as the visitor so
# one they may not open is not named, and what the post opens with, which is what puts the lock on
# a card. `effective_permissions` reads nothing while no category of the site is locked. A line in
# a sidebar draws none of it, so it reads none of it.

MishkaBlog.BlogPost
|> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
|> narrow(asked, source)
|> Ash.Query.sort(published_at: direction(asked.sort), id: :asc)
|> Ash.Query.select([
  :id,
  :title,
  :slug,
  :language,
  :excerpt,
  :published_at,
  :featured_image_url,
  :featured,
  :reading_time_minutes
])
|> with_card(asked.variant)
|> Ash.read(
  tenant: site_id(),
  page: [limit: per_page, offset: (page - 1) * per_page, count: total == :error]
)
|> paged()
|> case do
  {:ok, found} when is_map(found) ->
    case total do
      {:ok, counted} -> {:ok, %{found | total: counted}}
      :error -> {:ok, found}
    end

  unreadable ->
    unreadable
end

helpers.name: shared_page
helpers.code:
# THE PAGE OF POSTS THIS LIST WOULD READ, out of the page's own rows, where nothing narrows the list
# but what the page read them for — its language, the category or the tag it is of, and on the
# front page the strip's posts left out — in the order the page reads them, newest first, drawn as
# cards. `:error` for any other, which is read here.
plain? =
  asked.search == "" and not asked.featured_only and asked.exclude_slug == "" and
    asked.sort in ["", "newest"] and asked.variant != "compact"

case plain? do
  true ->
    shared(
      source,
      {:listed, asked.collection, asked.tag, asked.exclude_featured, per_page, page, asked.language}
    )

  false ->
    :error
end

helpers.name: shared_total
helpers.code:
# THE NUMBER OF POSTS THIS LIST HOLDS, out of the page's own rows, where the list is narrowed by
# nothing but what the page counted for: its language, and the category or the tag the page is of —
# the number its search box says too. On the front page the list leaves out the strip's featured
# posts, which are among the ones counted, so it holds that many fewer. `:error` for a list narrowed
# by anything else, which counts its own.
plain? = asked.search == "" and not asked.featured_only and asked.exclude_slug == ""

case {plain?, asked.exclude_featured} do
  {false, _excluded} ->
    :error

  {true, 0} ->
    shared(source, {:total, asked.collection, asked.tag, asked.language})

  {true, count} when asked.collection == "" and asked.tag == "" ->
    with {:ok, total} <- shared(source, {:total, "", "", asked.language}),
         {:ok, strip} <- shared(source, {:featured, count, asked.language}) do
      {:ok, max(total - length(strip), 0)}
    end

  {true, _excluded} ->
    :error
end

helpers.name: asked
helpers.code:
# EVERYTHING THE READ DEPENDS ON, AS ONE TERM — AND EVERYTHING A ROW IS DRAWN FROM, which is the
# same term for a reason. It is the argument the task is handed — a plain map rather than the
# socket, so nothing of LiveView's is copied into another process — and it is also what says
# whether anything has to be read at all: `update_many/1` runs on every render of the page holding
# this block, and a block that re-read on each of them would restart its own load whenever
# something else on the page moved.
#
# A STREAMED ROW IS RENDERED ONCE AND NEVER AGAIN. LiveView prunes `stream.inserts` after each
# render, so `@streams.posts` is empty on every render that is not a fresh load and the rows
# already on the page are never rebuilt. An attribute the ROWS read — the variant they are laid out

# RUN IN THE TASK, so nothing here may touch the socket. A page nobody has is a missing page when the
# address named it, and is clamped to the last one there is when the pager's buttons asked for it. The answer carries the term it was read for — `arrived/2` stores that rather than
# what was asked, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(asked, asked.page, asked.per_page, source) do
  pages = max(ceil(total / asked.per_page), 1)

  cond do
    asked.page <= pages ->
      {:ok,
       %{
         asked: asked,
         page: asked.page,
         posts: posts,
         total: total,
         pages: pages,
         filter_row: filter_row(asked, source),
         chips: chip_rows(asked)

    true ->

         %{
           asked: %{asked | page: pages},
           page: pages,
           posts: clamped,
           total: total,
           pages: pages,
           filter_row: filter_row(asked, source),

      end
  end
end

|> Enum.with_index()

    socket

# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not

      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path

helpers.name: narrow_to
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

# THE ROW A CATEGORY'S OR A TAG'S PAGE IS OF, as `blog-post-list` narrows by it. A slug names one
# category or tag per site whatever language it is written in, so it is the page's language that
# picks the edition of it, and `all` or no language narrows by the slug alone. A category counts only
# while it is active. Empty narrows nothing.
query =
  case {collection, language} do
    {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
      query

    {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
      Ash.Query.filter(
        query,
        exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active and language == ^code)
      )

    {wanted, _every_language} ->
      Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(collections, slug == ^wanted and status == :active))
  end

case {tag, language} do
  {"", _the_whole_archive} ->
    query

  {wanted, code} when code not in ["", "all"] ->
    Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted and language == ^code))

  {wanted, _every_language} ->
    Ash.Query.filter(query, exists(tags, slug == ^wanted))
end

helpers.name: count_posts
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

# EVERY POST THE READER MAY OPEN IN THIS EDITION, which is the number the search box says it will
# look through. Read as the visitor, so a locked post is not counted for one who cannot open it, and
# through the public read, so a draft, a scheduled post and an archived one are not counted at all.
# On a category's page or a tag's it is that category's or that tag's, narrowed as the list under it
# is (`narrow_to/4`), so the bar and the list's pager are counting from the same posts.
#
# THE PAGE COUNTED THEM ONCE, for this box and for the list under it, and where it handed the count
# down for this reader it is not counted again. Else the count comes with a read of one row, through
# the read itself: what keeps a post from a reader is a filter the read puts on as it runs, which a
# count of its own would not.
case shared(source, {:total, collection, tag, trimmed(language)}) do
  {:ok, count} ->
    count

  :error ->
    MishkaBlog.BlogPost
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
    |> narrow_language(language)
    |> narrow_to(collection, tag, language)
    |> Ash.Query.select([:id])
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1, count: true])
    |> case do
      {:ok, %{count: count}} when is_integer(count) -> count
      _unreadable -> 0
    end
end

# WHAT THE BAR CARRIES THROUGH A SEARCH, so searching inside a tag stays inside it: every key the
# page handed over but the words themselves and the page number, which a new search starts again.
case params do
  map when is_map(map) ->
    for {key, value} <- map,
        is_binary(value),
        key not in ["q", "page"],
        do: {key, value}

  _not_a_map ->
    []
end

helpers.name: update
helpers.code:
# THE COUNT IS READ ONCE FOR WHAT IT DEPENDS ON — who is looking, in which edition and of which
# category or tag — and not on every render of the page around it: this runs each time the page
# does, and a count that was asked again for nothing would be a query on every re-render. Only the
# bar draws it.
asked =
  {socket.assigns[:current_user], trimmed(socket.assigns[:language]),
   trimmed(socket.assigns[:collection]), trimmed(socket.assigns[:tag])}

case {trimmed(socket.assigns[:variant]), socket.assigns[:counted]} do
  {"bar", ^asked} ->
    {:ok, socket}

  {"bar", _before} ->
    {visitor, language, collection, tag} = asked

    {:ok,
     Phoenix.Component.assign(socket,
       counted: asked,
       total_posts: count_posts(source_of(socket.assigns), language, collection, tag, visitor)
     )}

  _no_bar ->
    {:ok, socket}
end

# THE VISITOR THE READ IS FOR, AS ITS ACTOR, so a post, a category or a tag locked to permissions
# it does not hold is left out of the rows, the count and the pages by the public action's own rules,
# and a page with nobody signed in reads as a guest. The tenant goes with it, because a public action

helpers.name: source_of
helpers.code:
# THE ROWS THE PAGE READ FOR THIS ADDRESS, when it handed them down (`page_source`) and read them for
# this block's reader on this block's site; `nil` otherwise, and the block reads for itself. Read by
# their shape, the one the extension's page source documents: a block calls nothing of its code.
site = site_id()

visitor =
  case assigns[:current_user] do
    %{id: id} -> id
    _guest -> nil
  end

case assigns[:page_source] do
  %{rows_of: "mishka_blog", site_id: ^site, visitor: ^visitor} = source -> source
  _not_for_this_block -> nil
end

helpers.name: shared
trimmed
helpers.code:
case value do
  binary when is_binary(binary) -> String.trim(binary)
  nil -> ""
  other -> to_string(other)
end

helpers.name: slug_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

helpers.name: permalink
helpers.code:
# THE POST'S OWN PAGE, offered while it is read beside a list — a list of its one address, or empty
# where there is no such page: no `post_base`, no `base` it is read beside, or a post in a language
# this site does not publish (`slug_href/4`). A permalink with nowhere to lead is not drawn.
case {trimmed(post_base), trimmed(base)} do
  {"", _beside} -> []
  {_own_page, ""} -> []
  {own_page, _beside} -> List.wrap(slug_href(own_page, post.slug, lang_param, post.language))
end

case assigns[:params] do

helpers.name: from_url?
helpers.code:
# WHETHER THE ADDRESS ASKED FOR THIS POST, or an author did. `asked_slug/1` prefers the URL's own
# capture and falls back to the `slug` attribute; only the first is the page's subject, and only the
# page's subject decides what the response is.
key = to_string(assigns[:post_param] || "post")

match?(%{^key => _asked}, assigns[:params])

helpers.name: missing!
helpers.code:
# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

  code when code in ~w(fa ar he ur ps ckb dv yi) -> "rtl"
  _left_to_right_or_unknown -> "auto"
end

helpers.name: body_html
helpers.code:
# STORED CONTENT WAS SANITIZED WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and is drawn as it was stored: a code-heavy
# post is hundreds of kilobytes of highlighted spans, and scrubbing it again cost every view of it
# ~150 ms. What a render_content plugin changed was never scrubbed, so that alone is sanitized here.
# `rich_content` draws the HTML as it is given, and each component marker in it as the component it
# names.
cond do
  not is_binary(rendered) -> ""
  rendered == content -> rendered
  true -> HtmlSanitizeEx.html5(rendered)
end

helpers.name: only_language
helpers.code:
# A PAGE WRITTEN IN ONE LANGUAGE SERVES THAT LANGUAGE'S EDITION AND NO OTHER. A slug belongs to one
# edition, so without this /fa/blog/<english-slug> answers the English article inside a Persian,
# right-to-left page, with a Persian sidebar around it and nothing saying the URL was wrong. Left
# empty the component sits on a page that does not address languages at all, and the slug decides on
# its own.
require Ash.Query

case trimmed(wanted) do
  "" -> query
  "all" -> query
  code -> Ash.Query.filter(query, language == ^code)
end

helpers.name: load_post
helpers.code:
require Ash.Query

assigns = socket.assigns
slug = asked_slug(assigns)

post =
  case slug in [nil, ""] do
    true ->
      nil

    false ->
      asked = {:record, "blog:post", to_string(slug), trimmed(assigns[:language])}

      case shared(source_of(assigns), asked) do
        {:ok, row} -> row
        :error -> read_post(slug, assigns)
      end
  end

# A SLUG THE URL NAMED AND NOTHING ANSWERS IS A MISSING PAGE, not a page with a notice on it.
# The address was a post; there is no post; 404 is the honest answer and the one a crawler needs —
# see `MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError`, which every other "not here" in this CMS
# raises. LiveView converts it exactly as a controller does: on the HTTP render Phoenix's error view
# draws the 404 page, and on a connected render the client reloads into that same answer.
#
# ONLY WHEN THE URL NAMED IT. A slug an author typed into the `slug` attribute of an embedded card
# is their content mistake, and taking the whole page down for it would be a worse answer than the
# notice — so that case still draws `missing_text`.
if post == nil and slug not in [nil, ""] and from_url?(assigns) do
  missing!(socket)
end

# NOTHING IS READ FOR A PART THE PAGE TURNED OFF. `update/2` runs again on every re-render of the
# page holding this component, so a page drawing the body alone paid for three reads it never showed,
# every single time.
socket
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:slug, slug)
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:post, post)
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:locked, locked?(post))
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:tags, (assigns[:show_tags] && tags_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:categories, (assigns[:show_categories] && categories_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])
|> Phoenix.Component.assign(:authors, (assigns[:show_authors] && authors_of(post, assigns[:current_user])) || [])

helpers.name: read_post
helpers.code:
# THE POST THE SLUG NAMES, read here, as the visitor, where the page handed no rows of its own for
# it.
require Ash.Query

MishkaBlog.BlogPost
|> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(assigns[:current_user]))
|> Ash.Query.filter(slug == ^to_string(slug))
|> only_language(assigns[:language])
|> Ash.Query.select([
  :id,
  :title,
  :subtitle,
  :slug,
  :excerpt,
  :content,
  :published_at,
  :updated_at,
  :featured_image_url,
  :featured,
  :language,
  :language_group_id,
  :reading_time_minutes
])
|> Ash.Query.load([:rendered_content, :effective_permissions])
|> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1])
|> first_row()

# a module out of (component name, site name). Every `<.component …/>` below draws a sibling of this
# one, which lives on the same site as this one and nowhere else.

# THE ROWS `blog-term-row` DRAWS, prepared here because only this block knows which base each
# kind of row is addressed under. A base nobody gave means a word rather than a link, which is what
# a block that does not own the router can honestly offer. Neither kind ever patches: a category
# and a tag lead to a page of their own or to nothing.

# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.

      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path

# are. Each is counted as its own page counts it — its published posts in its language that the
# visitor may open (`listed_post_count`) — in the same statement, and its latest posts are read with
# it (`latest_posts/2`), as the visitor.
query =
  MishkaBlog.Collection
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(asked.visitor))
  |> narrow_language(asked.language)
  |> Ash.Query.sort(display_order: :asc, name: :asc)
  |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name, :slug, :language, :description])
  |> Ash.Query.load(:listed_post_count)
  |> latest_posts(asked)

query =
  case asked.hide_empty do
    false -> query
    true -> with_public_post(query, asked.language)
  end

page = [limit: asked.limit]

found =
  case asked.parent do
    "all" ->
      query |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: page) |> rows()

    "" ->
      query
      |> Ash.Query.filter(is_nil(parent_collection_id))
      |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: page)
      |> rows()

    wanted ->
      case parent_row(wanted, asked.language, asked.visitor) do
        nil ->
          {:ok, []}

        parent ->
          query
          |> Ash.Query.filter(parent_collection_id == ^parent.id)
          |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: page)
          |> rows()
      end
  end

with {:ok, found} <- found do
  {:ok,
   %{
     categories:
       Enum.map(found, fn category ->
         %{
           id: category.id,
           name: category.name,
           slug: category.slug,
           language: category.language,
           description: category.description,
           count: category.listed_post_count,
           posts: posts_of(category)
         }
       end)
   }}
end

require Ash.Query

# THE REPLIES ARE READ AS THE COMMENTS ABOVE THEM ARE, through the public action and as the
# visitor. `replies` itself reads through the resource's primary action, which is the moderators'.
replies =
  MishkaBlog.Comment
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(visitor))
  |> Ash.Query.load(:rendered_content)

# ONE CAPPED PAGE AT A TIME. `:approved_by_post` hands back at most 100 rows and Ash shrinks a
# bigger ask to that cap rather than refusing it, so asking for the whole conversation at once made
# every comment past the hundredth unreachable while "load more" stayed on the page for ever.
#
# ONE ROW MORE THAN IS SHOWN SAYS WHETHER THERE ARE MORE, which is all "load more" asks: a count of
# every top-level comment beside the rows was a second read of the same comments.
probe = wanted + 1

Enum.reduce_while(Stream.iterate(0, &(&1 + 100)), {:ok, []}, fn offset, {:ok, gathered} ->
  ask = min(probe - offset, 100)

  MishkaBlog.Comment
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:approved_by_post, %{post_id: post_id}, read_as(visitor))
  |> Ash.Query.filter(is_nil(parent_comment_id))
  |> Ash.Query.sort(is_pinned: :desc, inserted_at: :asc)
  |> Ash.Query.load([:rendered_content, replies: replies])
  |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: ask, offset: offset])
  |> paged()
  |> case do
    {:error, reason} ->
      {:halt, {:error, reason}}

    {:ok, %{rows: page}} ->
      rows = gathered ++ page

      case length(rows) < probe and length(page) == ask do
        true -> {:cont, {:ok, rows}}
        false -> {:halt, {:ok, rows}}
      end
  end
end)
|> case do
  {:ok, rows} -> {:ok, {Enum.take(rows, wanted), length(rows) > wanted}}
  {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
end

# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every

asked = asked(socket.assigns)
# THE PAGE'S OWN ROWS GO WITH THE READ, into the task too, which has no socket to find them on.
source = source_of(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked, source))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:comments, fn -> fetch(asked, source) end)
    end
end

require Ash.Query

case post do
  %{approved_comment_count: count} when is_integer(count) ->
    count

  # ONE READ OF ONE ROW, which carries the count Ash works out for the whole of the approved ones,
  # through the read itself: what keeps a comment to its reader is a filter the read puts on as it
  # runs, which a count of its own would not.
  %{id: post_id} ->
    MishkaBlog.Comment
    |> Ash.Query.for_read(:approved_by_post, %{post_id: post_id}, read_as(visitor))
    |> Ash.read(tenant: site_id(), page: [limit: 1, count: true])
    |> case do
      {:ok, %{count: count}} when is_integer(count) -> count
      _unreadable -> drawn
    end
end

helpers.code:
# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

helpers.name: slug_href
helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

# site's first.
case trimmed(language) do
  code when code in ["", "all"] -> MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.Languages.primary(site_id())
  code -> code
end

# page's language is not one this site publishes (`slug_href/4`) — so the template draws that row as
# a word rather than as a link to nothing.
case trimmed(base) do
  "" ->
    Enum.map(rows, &{&1, nil})

  address ->
    code = link_language(language)
    Enum.map(rows, &{&1, slug_href(address, &1.slug, lang_param, code)})
end

require Ash.Query

# THE CATEGORIES EACH CARD NAMES, read as the visitor in one query for the whole page of posts rather
# than one per card, and only the two columns the card draws.
categories =
  MishkaBlog.Collection
  |> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(listed.visitor))
  |> Ash.Query.sort(display_order: :asc, name: :asc)
  |> Ash.Query.select([:id, :name])

MishkaBlog.BlogPost
|> Ash.Query.for_read(:public_list, %{}, read_as(listed.visitor))
|> narrow_language(listed.language)
|> Ash.Query.filter(exists(bloggers, slug == ^listed.slug and is_nil(archived_at)))
|> Ash.Query.sort(published_at: :desc)
|> Ash.Query.select([
  :id,
  :title,
  :slug,
  :language,
  :excerpt,
  :published_at,
  :featured_image_url,
  :featured
])
|> Ash.Query.load(collections: categories)
|> Ash.read(

  page: [limit: listed.per_page, offset: (page - 1) * listed.per_page, count: true]

helpers.name: fetch_posts
helpers.code:
# A PAGE NOBODY HAS IS A MISSING PAGE when the address named it, and is clamped to the last one there
# is when the pager's buttons asked for it. The answer carries the term it was read
# for, as the list's does, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
case listed.wanted and listed.slug != "" do
  false ->
    {:ok, %{listed: listed, posts: [], page: 1, pages: 1, total: nil}}

  true ->
    with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(listed, listed.page) do
      pages = max(ceil(total / listed.per_page), 1)

      cond do
        listed.page <= pages ->
          {:ok,
           %{listed: listed, posts: posts, page: listed.page, pages: pages, total: total}}

        listed.page_in_url ->
          {:missing, listed}

        true ->
          with {:ok, %{rows: clamped}} <- posts_page(listed, pages) do
            {:ok,
             %{
               listed: %{listed | page: pages},
               posts: clamped,
               page: pages,
               pages: pages,
               total: total
             }}
          end
      end
    end
end

# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.

helpers.name: load_profile
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)
# THE PAGE'S OWN ROWS GO WITH THE READ, into the task too, which has no socket to find them on.
source = source_of(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked, source))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:profile, fn -> fetch(asked, source) end)
    end
end

# NOTHING ANSWERS AT AN ADDRESS THAT NAMED SOMETHING. On the very first render there is no socket
# to send anything over, so this raises and Phoenix draws the 404 page with a 404 status, exactly as
# it does for a controller.
#
# ONCE CONNECTED IT ASKS THE PAGE TO ASK AGAIN. Raising into a live render crashes the view, and on
# a `patch` the client remounts straight back into the same missing subject and crashes again. A
# LiveComponent has no `handle_params/3` of its own, so it tells the LiveView the way the guides say
# to — `send/2` — and `MishkaCmsWeb.Live.RuntimeLive` answers with a full load of the same address,
# which arrives here as the first-render case above.
if Phoenix.LiveView.connected?(socket) do
  # THE PAGE KNOWS ITS OWN ADDRESS AND THIS DOES NOT: a LiveComponent's assigns are its own, not
  # the LiveView's, so the message carries nothing and the answer is given where the path lives.
  send(self(), :mishka_runtime_not_found)
  socket
else
  raise MishkaCmsCore.ErrorsExceptions.NotFoundError,
    message: "Sorry, the page you are looking for does not exist or has been moved."
end

helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

helpers.name: fetch_posts
helpers.code:
# A PAGE NOBODY HAS IS A MISSING PAGE when the address named it, and is clamped to the last one there
# is when the pager's buttons asked for it. The answer carries the term it was read
# for, as the list's does, so a clamp settles instead of asking again on the next render.
case listed.wanted and listed.slug != "" do
  false ->
    {:ok, %{listed: listed, posts: [], page: 1, pages: 1, total: nil}}

  true ->
    with {:ok, %{rows: posts, total: total}} <- posts_page(listed, listed.page) do
      pages = max(ceil(total / listed.per_page), 1)

      cond do
        listed.page <= pages ->
          {:ok,
           %{listed: listed, posts: posts, page: listed.page, pages: pages, total: total}}

        listed.page_in_url ->
          {:missing, listed}

        true ->
          with {:ok, %{rows: clamped}} <- posts_page(listed, pages) do
            {:ok,
             %{
               listed: %{listed | page: pages},
               posts: clamped,
               page: pages,
               pages: pages,
               total: total
             }}
          end
      end
    end
end

helpers.code:
# THE ADDRESS OF A ROW, built by `site_path/2`: a `:lang` in the base is filled with the language of
# the row being linked to, not the one the page is read in, and the address is the one the site's
# URL mode gives that language — `/blog/<slug>` in a first language the site leaves unprefixed,
# `/fa/blog/<slug>` in Persian. A base without the segment is filled as written, and a query-mode
# page carries the language in `lang_param` instead. A row whose language this site does not
# publish, or cannot be read, gets no link rather than a link to a 404.
case site_path(to_string(base) <> "/:slug", %{"lang" => trimmed(language), "slug" => to_string(slug)}) do
  nil ->
    nil

  path ->
    case {trimmed(lang_param), trimmed(language)} do
      {"", _no_key} -> path
      {_key, ""} -> path
      {key, code} -> path <> "?" <> URI.encode_query(%{key => code})
    end
end

  code when code in ["", "all"] -> MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.Languages.primary(site_id())

# rather than the socket, so nothing of LiveView's is copied into another process — and it is also

# holding this block, and a block that re-read on each of them would restart its own load whenever

helpers.name: cold?
helpers.code:
# NO PROCESS AT ALL, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS NOT CONNECTED. `connected?/1` answers false twice:
# on the builder's canvas and the Preview, where `MishkaCmsCore.Runtime.LiveViewHelpers.cold/2`
# renders this block with no LiveView behind it, and on the first HTTP render of a real page, where
# there IS a process and the socket connects a moment later. Only the first has nobody to hand a
# task's answer to; the second must NOT read here, or the page's HTTP response waits for every
# block on it and then throws the rows away, because the mount that follows reads them again.

helpers.name: load
helpers.code:
asked = asked(socket.assigns)

case socket.assigns[:asked] do
  ^asked ->
    socket

  before ->
    socket = Phoenix.Component.assign(socket, :asked, asked)

    case cold?(socket) or is_nil(before) do
      true ->
        arrived(socket, fetch(asked))

      false ->
        socket
        |> Phoenix.Component.assign(loading: true, failed: false)
        |> MishkaGervaz.Messages.start_async(:people, fn -> fetch(asked) end)
    end
end

components.name: blog-profile-card
components.description: A function component: one blogger or one team as a tile (picture, name, handle and a line about them), as a small pill, or as the picture alone at one of four sizes or any size the caller sets. The picture is theirs, or their letters on a tint their slug picks, so a person is the same colour on every page. Drawn by blog-author-profile, blog-team-profile and blog-people, and as the picture alone by blog-post-card and blog-post-detail for the people who wrote a post.

<.link :if={@navigate} navigate={@navigate} data-role="blog-profile-name" dir="auto" class="text-[15px] font-medium after:absolute after:inset-0" > {@name} {@name} @{@handle} ·  {@count_text}

opts.doc: The name to draw — a blogger's, a team's. Nothing is drawn without one: this component holds no query of its own.

The slug drawn under the name, as @handle. Left empty, none is drawn. It also picks the tint of the letters, so give it wherever the person is drawn and they keep one colour — on a card's byline, on a post, on their own page.
The address of their picture. Left empty, the first letters of the name are drawn on a tint of their own, the same tint wherever this person is drawn.
A line about them, a blogger's bio or a team's description, drawn as plain text and cut at two lines. Left empty, none is drawn.

card draws the picture, the name, the handle and the line about them as a bordered tile; compact draws a small picture and the name in a pill, which is what a row of teams wants; avatar draws the picture alone, the way a stack of faces or a profile's head does.
Where the name leads — their own page. Left empty it is drawn as a word, not a link.
The data-role the card carries, so the block around it names its own rows — blog-team-member, say.
What follows the handle on the card, already counted and in the reader's words: 5 posts, say. Left empty, none is drawn.
The card's own background: card is the page's white surface, sunk is the slightly recessed one for a tile that sits on a surface already.

How large the picture is when variant is avatar: xs 24px, sm 36px, md 46px, lg 112px. custom draws no box of its own — the size, the lettering and the shape come from class, which is how the byline of a card and the head of a post draw the same person at the sizes their designs set.
Overlap the picture with the next one and ring it in the surface colour, so a row of avatars reads as a stack of faces.
Classes the picture takes on top of its tint, which is what a size of custom is sized and lettered with. Only the avatar variant reads it.
The name is written beside the picture already, so the picture says nothing of its own: its alt is empty. Only the avatar variant reads it.

helpers.name: plain
helpers.code:
# PLAIN TEXT, because a line on a card is not the place for a bio's links and emphasis: what was
# stored is drawn without its tags, its whitespace folded.
case value do
  text when is_binary(text) ->
    text
    |> HtmlSanitizeEx.strip_tags()
    |> String.replace(~r/\s+/u, " ")
    |> String.trim()

  _nothing -> ""
end

helpers.name: initials
helpers.code:
# THE FIRST LETTER OF EACH OF THE FIRST TWO WORDS, as the design draws a person: Alice Smith is AS.
# A one-word name, and a team's, is its first letter alone.
name
|> to_string()
|> String.split(~r/\s+/u, trim: true)
|> Enum.take(2)
|> Enum.map_join(&String.first/1)
|> String.upcase()

helpers.name: seed
helpers.code:
# WHAT PICKS THE TINT, so the same person has the same colour on the people page, on their own page
# and on their team's: the slug where there is one, the name where the caller has none to give.
case trimmed(handle) do
  "" -> trimmed(name)
  slug -> slug
end

helpers.name: tint
helpers.code:
# THE SIX TINTS OF THE SITE'S THEME (`tint-1` to `tint-6`), each as the whole of its classes. One clause per tint rather than a
# class built from an index, because Tailwind reads source text and a class with a hole in it gets
# no rule: the per-site compiler scans these literals, which is the only reason they colour anything.
case :erlang.phash2(to_string(seed), 6) do
  0 -> "bg-tint-1 text-tint-1-ink dark:bg-tint-1-dark dark:text-tint-1-ink-dark"
  1 -> "bg-tint-2 text-tint-2-ink dark:bg-tint-2-dark dark:text-tint-2-ink-dark"
  2 -> "bg-tint-3 text-tint-3-ink dark:bg-tint-3-dark dark:text-tint-3-ink-dark"
  3 -> "bg-tint-4 text-tint-4-ink dark:bg-tint-4-dark dark:text-tint-4-ink-dark"
  4 -> "bg-tint-5 text-tint-5-ink dark:bg-tint-5-dark dark:text-tint-5-ink-dark"
  _ -> "bg-tint-6 text-tint-6-ink dark:bg-tint-6-dark dark:text-tint-6-ink-dark"
end

stylesheets.name: blog-code-highlight
stylesheets.description: Colours the code blocks in a post: pre.highlight and the token classes Makeup emits, in its Monokai style.
stylesheets.content:
/* Code in a blog post: <pre class="highlight"><code class="language-x"> with one <span> per token.
   The token classes are the ones Makeup emits, coloured in its Monokai style. */
pre.highlight {
  color: #f8f8f2;
  background-color: #272822;
  border-radius: 12px;
  padding: 16px 20px;
  margin: 0 0 12px;
  overflow-x: auto;
  font-size: 13px;
  line-height: 1.6;
  direction: ltr;
  text-align: left;
  tab-size: 2;
}

pre.highlight code {
  display: block;
  padding: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: inherit;
  font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace;
  font-size: inherit;
  white-space: pre;
}
